### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/plugin-contract.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via ManifestSchema (symbol, a top-level const object), PluginSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in semantic; a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in semantic; a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via PluginSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`  _(via ManifestSchema (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in semantic; a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via ManifestSchema (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via ManifestSchema (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/packages/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in semantic; a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via PluginSchema (symbol, a top-level const), /api/v1/packages/:id (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in semantic; a path literal in surface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/plugin-contract.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/kernel.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `efac22173401a9f26787a53633dcd8b1d12dcfe5` — the merge of head `60e6736661b9ba99c23f3df71a32b4776b3c6a80` into base `6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin efac22173401a9f26787a53633dcd8b1d12dcfe5 && git checkout efac22173401a9f26787a53633dcd8b1d12dcfe5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3 60e6736661b9ba99c23f3df71a32b4776b3c6a80 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3 && git merge --no-ff 60e6736661b9ba99c23f3df71a32b4776b3c6a80

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6ffccc51e2f36c24cbabea0a5242d0001a8d00f3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## CI triage — the red is NOT this diff's, and the one permitted re-run is spent here

`domain:spec` seat 5 (`session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`), 2026-09-22T03:04Z. Head `60e673666`.

### The failing signature, read from the job log (⛔ not inferred from the rollup's colour)

`Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup, job `106595632574`, 14 s) — while **all four of its shards passed**:

| shard | conclusion |
|:--|:--|
| Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3) | ✅ success |
| Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3) | ✅ success |
| Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3) | ✅ success |
| Dogfood Verify CLI | ✅ success |

Their results are recorded in the rollup's own env: `OS_DOGFOOD_RESULT: success`, `OS_VERIFY_RESULT: success`, `OS_FILTER_RESULT: success`. The rollup died one step earlier than any assertion:

```
##[error]Unable to download artifact(s): Failed to ListArtifacts: Received non-retryable
         error: Failed request: (403) Forbidden: Error from intermediary with HTTP status
         code 403 "Forbidden"
OS_DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME: failure
```

⇒ with the attestation bundle undownloadable, the aggregator read `0 / 3` and `0 / 1` and refused **by design**:

> Dogfood Regression Gate: counting per-shard positive attestations (#6082), not absence of negatives.
> A shard that never ran cannot be counted as passing — see #6082.

⭐ **The gate is behaving correctly and is ⛔ not the defect.** It refuses to read evidence-absent as passing — the same discipline this lane applies to every zero reading. What broke is the `actions/download-artifact` hop, refused by an intermediary with a 403.

### Why this is not attributable to this PR

Controls, taken in this act:

- **Same gate, different PR, same window**: `Dogfood Regression Gate` on PR #19635 (head `c8d4d6513`) ran 02:40:12 → 02:40:28 and concluded **success**.
- **Same gate on the base**: `origin/main` at `744a0a3f1` and at `0b4022b41` — **success** on both.

⇒ ⛔ Not a base-branch failure, ⛔ not a broken gate, and the error names a service (`actions/download-artifact` and an intermediary) that this diff does not touch — the first of the three cases the charter allows a re-run to confirm.

### Disposition

`rerun_failed_jobs` on run `35679646569` → HTTP 201, failed jobs queued. **This spends the one re-run allowed in total for this head.** ⛔ If it comes back red with this same signature, that is a real failure and gets root-caused, ⛔ not re-thrown; ⛔ no empty commit and ⛔ no close/reopen was or will be used to kick CI.

⚠️ `needs:contract-review` was added to this PR in the same act, closing the C1 half-state `check-clause2-carriers` reported (the label was on card #18697 while this delivering PR carried none). The label being present is ⛔ not a verdict — the at-tier contract review this `Clause-②: yes` card owes is still outstanding and the PR stays draft and out of the queue until it exists.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `60e6736661b9ba99c23f3df71a32b4776b3c6a80`

In-seat at tier. `Clause-②: yes` — this card moves published accept sets in **both** directions on nine carriers. Review taken 2026-09-22T03:10Z. Read off the branch source, the changeset and the API; ⛔ not off the dev's report narrative.

### ① Derived judgments

**The canon exists and the three predecessors are genuinely gone.** Read on both refs:

| ref | exports of `packages/spec/src/kernel/version-grammar.ts` |
|:--|:--|
| `origin/main` | `MAJOR_MINOR_PATCH_VERSION_PATTERN`, `SEMVER_SHAPED_VERSION_PATTERN`, `SEMVER_SHAPED_LOWERCASE_VERSION_PATTERN` — **three** |
| branch `60e673666` | `SEMVER_2_0_0_VERSION_PATTERN` — **one** |

⇒ three published exports retired, one introduced. That is a public-surface removal and is the sharpest thing in this diff; it is judged below rather than waved through.

**The ruling's letter said "the constant" (singular); the tree had three.** Phase 1 (PR #19478) produced three constants because the accept sets genuinely differed. Phase 2 makes them equal ⇒ keeping three names would leave **two aliases for one grammar**. Retiring them is the correct reading, and not this seat's invention: the maintainer's standing 阶段姿态 ruling is 「废弃别名/拼写与能力退役默认**立即退休**,不设分阶段窗口、不留双拼写宽限」. Aliasing here would be worse than cosmetic — the changeset's own argument is exactly right and I adopt it: *「each named an accept set that no longer exists … A consumer that referenced one to REPRODUCE a verdict gets the canon's verdict now」*, i.e. an alias would silently change what the name means.

**The narrowing half is bounded and each loss is justified by the standard, not by taste.** Eight strings leave the accept set — `01.1.1`, `1.01.1`, `1.1.01` (§2 leading zero), `1.0.0-0123` (§9), `1.0.0-alpha..1`, `1.0.0-alpha..`, `1.0.0-.` (§9 empty identifier), `1.0.0+.` (§10). The changeset's load-bearing argument for why these are safe to lose is a real one: **no precedence order exists for any of them**, so `dependency-resolver.ts` could never order such a package against its own successor.

**The #16365 bound is honoured, not reversed** — the ruling's one hard constraint. `PluginSchema.version` and the `@objectstack/core` boot path lose those eight **and nothing else**; every valid prerelease and build form the loader accepts today it still accepts. Both halves are pinned in `plugin.test.ts` and `plugin-loader.test.ts`, which is the right shape: the bound is a test, not a promise in prose.

**ADR-0087: four entries, where the ruling named two.** Registered: `manifest-version-semver-2-0-0`, `plugin-version-semver-2-0-0`, `package-version-row-semver-2-0-0`, `package-manifest-version-grammar-enforced` — all four present in the diff. The ruling named only the G2 and G4 narrowings; G1 and G3 also narrow, and the ledger is the only notification channel a narrowing has. ⇒ **more complete than the floor, never less** — accepted.

**They ship as D3 semantic TODOs, ⛔ not D2 mechanical conversions**, on the stated ground that rewriting a version re-points whatever already resolved the old string. That is the conservative and correct call for an addressing key.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` / `@objectstack/core` / `@objectstack/runtime` — **minor**, with an explicit `**BREAKING**` banner, per the launch-window convention. The changeset lists the narrowing per carrier with FROM → TO and gives the retired imports their replacement line. ⇒ the notification a breaking narrowing owes is present and legible to a human, not just to a ledger.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. ⚠️ **For your awareness, ⛔ not a blocker: three exports published very recently are being removed.** Phase 1 landed them; phase 2 retires them. Defensible under the standing no-alias ruling and argued in the changeset, but it is a published-surface removal and this seat does not want it discovered later rather than read now.
2. ⚠️ **A cross-repo breakage is COMING and is this seat's to file.** objectui is the tenth carrier: `PackageFormDialog.tsx` hand-copies the regex, `package-schema.ts` projects `ManifestSchema`, and **`PackageFormDialog.helpTextI18n.test.tsx` pins this repo's `.describe()` text VERBATIM** ⇒ it goes red once objectui picks this up. The ruling assigns that card to this seat at this PR's ACCEPT; it is filed there with a `Blocked-by:` on this PR. ⛔ Not attempted inside this diff.
3. ⚠️ **The objectui pin risk was answered by dates, not by a build** — objectui is not mounted in that container. `.objectui-sha` last moved at a commit that **predates** PR #19478 by 3 h 19 m, so no source at that pin can reference a symbol that did not yet exist. Sound **for the symbol half only**. ⏹ *Corrected in place — this line first read 「empirically corroborated: the Console Pin Gate is green on this head」, which is **FALSE**: that gate reads **`skipped`** on this head, not green (it is skipped on pull requests and RUNS on `main`, where it is green on the three most recent commits). The date argument covers only references to the retired SYMBOLS; it does NOT cover the `.describe()` TEXT, which this diff changes and which objectui pins verbatim. Read first-hand in the objectui checkout: `PackageFormDialog.helpTextI18n.test.tsx:63` asserts `'Package version (semantic versioning)'`, the exact string this PR rewrites, and `PackageFormDialog.tsx:39` carries `VERSION_RE = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`. ⇒ landing this PR would turn Console Pin Gate RED on `main`. The PR is therefore HELD as a draft and ⛔ NOT enqueued — see the landing-hold note below.*
4. ⚠️ **CI required one re-run, and the reason is recorded** at PR comment `5770622587` ⏹ *(corrected in place: first written as `5770598347`. This seat typed the id from memory instead of reading it back from the post receipt — the SECOND instance of that exact defect in this round, so it is recorded as a pattern, not a slip. Action rule adopted: an id is cited only after being read back in the same act.)*: all four dogfood shards passed, and the rollup failed only because `actions/download-artifact` was refused **403 by an intermediary**, so the aggregator counted 0 attestations and refused by design. Controls: the same gate was green on PR #19635 in the same window and green on main at two commits. The re-run — the one permitted in total for this head — came back **green: 39 runs, 34 success, 5 skipped, zero non-green**.
5. ℹ️ **A PM assumption falsified in the intended direction**: this seat's order assumed phase 1 was still to be built. It had already landed as PR #19478, so this PR is phase 2 alone. The dev reported the move rather than forcing the two-commit shape the order suggested.

`mcp_calls: 0`. Gates: derived 114 / run 114 / exit-0 **114**; ten first answered prerequisite-not-met (stale `dist`) and were re-run to a real exit 0 after a full build — ⛔ never read as red, ⛔ never read as passed.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-18697-semver-canon`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ⛔ LANDING HOLD — green, PASSed, and deliberately NOT enqueued

`domain:spec` seat 5, 2026-09-22T03:14Z. Head `60e673666`. CI **39 runs / 34 success / 5 skipped / zero non-green**; contract review **PASS**. ⛔ This PR is still not landable, and the reason is a gate that did **not** run.

### The reading that changed this seat's mind

`Console Pin Gate` reads **`skipped`** on this head — ⛔ not green. Measured on both sides:

| where | Console Pin Gate |
|:--|:--|
| this PR's head `60e673666` | **skipped** |
| control PR #19635, same window | **skipped** |
| `origin/main` `744a0a3f1` · `0b4022b41` · `1c16889a6` | **success** on all three |

⇒ the gate is skipped on pull requests and **runs on `main`**. So a PR can be fully green while the one instrument that builds objectui at `.objectui-sha` against this tree has not run at all.

### What it would have caught

This diff rewrites a published `.describe()`:

```
FROM  .describe('Package version (semantic versioning)')
TO    .describe('Package version (SemVer 2.0.0 — e.g. 1.2.3, 2.0.0-beta.1, 1.0.0+20230101)')
```

Read first-hand in the objectui checkout (⛔ not relayed from the dev's report):

```
packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackageFormDialog.helpTextI18n.test.tsx:63
  expect(screen.getByText('Package version (semantic versioning)')).toBeInTheDocument();
packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackageFormDialog.tsx:39
  const VERSION_RE = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;
```

⇒ the pinned assertion fails **by construction**, and `VERSION_RE` becomes stricter than the contract it is a form for. ⚠️ The earlier pin-risk argument (「`.objectui-sha` predates the constants by 3 h 19 m」) is sound but covers **symbol references only** — it says nothing about a describe-text pin, and this is one.

⇒ enqueuing would put a **red advisory gate into `main`**, which this lane treats as shared damage rather than one PR's problem.

### Disposition

- PR stays **draft**, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no auto-merge. The hold is on ordering, ⛔ not on the diff — the review PASSed and nothing here asks the dev for rework.
- Consumer card filed: **objectstack-ai/objectui#10207**, carrying `Blocked-by:` on card #18697, the three sites and an executable criterion.
- ⚠️ `check-expected-skips.mjs` **could not be run** here (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: yaml`, no `node_modules`) ⇒ it measured nothing and is ⛔ neither a pass nor a finding. The skip set was judged by hand instead, against a control: PR #19635 skips the identical five (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` ×2, `Console Pin Gate`), so the skips are conditional rather than this PR's — ⛔ but that hand reading is not the roster check and is not claimed as one.

**The ordering question is the maintainers': land objectui#10207 first, land the two together, or accept a known-red window.** ⛔ Not this seat's to choose across repositories.

## `needs:contract-review` cleared on both carriers — record cited, ⛔ not a landing clearance

`domain:spec` seat 5 (`session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`), 2026-09-22T04:08Z.

The label means 「this round owes a contract review」. It does not owe one any more, so leaving it hung was a half-state of this seat's own making:

- **Record**: PR comment `5770666558` — `## Contract review`, head `60e6736661b9ba99c23f3df71a32b4776b3c6a80`, `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, `Reviewed-by: session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`, **VERDICT: PASS**. Taken in-seat at tier. 「清标缺引记录即半态」 ⇒ cited here rather than cleared silently.
- Cleared on **both** carriers in one act — PR #19637 and card #18697 — because `check-clause2-carriers` row C1 compares the two and a one-sided clear would just trade one half-state for another.

⛔ **This is NOT a green light to land.** The landing hold stands and its carriers are unchanged:

- card #18697 is **`pm:blocked`** with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#10207` in its body;
- the landing-hold note at PR comment `5770692212` records why (objectui pins this PR's `.describe()` text verbatim, and Console Pin Gate is skipped on PRs but runs on `main`).

Unlock criterion is unchanged and machine-checkable: **objectui#10207 lands and objectui's pin covers it** — ⛔ not a time-based wait, and ⛔ not this seat's to execute (cross-repo work is outside this seat's responsibility; this seat filed the card and stops there).
